solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dad's time: it was long ago?

parts.note: Dad is Pa, so Dad's is Pa's

explanation.surface: A wistful look back at father's era, wondering if it was all so long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever happened long ago belongs to bygone days, so the phrase describes that earlier time.

clue.text: Fish to cut up — not easy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for cut is written bottom to top

explanation.surface: Preparing a fish for the table is fiddly work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut up' reads like preparing the fish, but 'up' reverses CLIP to PILC, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, an adult sardine.

clue.text: Playwright in Irish: award-winner

indicators.note: in says the answer is found sitting inside the following words

explanation.surface: A playwright from Ireland who won a major prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside 'Irish award', and the surface is true: George Bernard Shaw was Irish and won the Nobel Prize.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw wrote Pygmalion and Saint Joan, among many stage works.

clue.text: Got hold of equipment, given guidance

parts.note: tack is a horse's equipment: saddle, bridle and so on

explanation.surface: Someone acquires the right gear after being shown what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle someone or something is to seize or grapple with it, physically taking hold.

clue.text: More than one politician attempts to convey love

indicators.note: to convey is to carry, so the word for attempts carries the letter for love inside it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Politicians trying to show some affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party, so the plural covers several politicians.

clue.text: Holiday resort on coast: clean, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of the preceding words turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A seaside resort turns out to be clean, much to visitors' surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the letters of 'on coast clean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clacton-on-Sea is a traditional seaside holiday town on the Essex coast of England.

clue.text: Evangelist not a hot-gospeller? Only mildly enthusiastic

definitions.meaning: playful reading: the evangelist ... but not hot, unlike a fiery preacher

explanation.surface: A preacher who lacks fire is barely enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the answer into Luke, one of the four Gospel writers, and warm, which falls short of hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid water is neither hot nor cold, and by extension a tepid response shows little keenness.

clue.text: Partner on an assignation offers fruit

definitions.meaning: the person you go out with on a romantic engagement
the sweet fruit of a palm tree

explanation.surface: Someone on a romantic outing brings along some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic companion for an evening out is called this, and it is also the palm's sticky brown fruit.

clue.text: Ideal joints for a worker?

parts.note: a worker bee's leg joints are literally its knees, and the idiom means something excellent

explanation.surface: What sort of joints would suit a labourer best?
explanation.walkthrough: A worker is the crossword's usual bee; its knees are its joints, and the idiom for the very best thing names exactly those.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes anything outstanding or perfect, matching ideal.

clue.text: Grub in part of biker's outfit

definitions.meaning: a larva, here of the crane fly

explanation.surface: Food found in the pocket of a motorcyclist's gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of the crane fly has a tough skin and the name of a hide coat worn by bikers.

clue.text: Extra word of farewell

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run scored when the ball passes the batter untouched is an extra of this kind
a short way of saying goodbye

explanation.surface: An additional parting word.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run scored without the bat touching the ball counts as an extra of this name; it also means goodbye.

clue.text: Various ideas in words selectively spoken to audience

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the next word are rearranged into a different form

explanation.surface: Different thoughts are voiced for some listeners only.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, a remark made for the audience to hear while other characters supposedly do not is this stage device.

clue.text: Editor excited about peoples' representative brought in

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the representative
excited suggests the letters of the word editor are stirred up

parts.note: MP is Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: An editor gets worked up about an MP being brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Editor' looks like the subject of the sentence but is anagram fodder: 'excited' gives IORTED, which 'about' wraps round the MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods brought in from abroad are described with this word, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Space for luggage men needed in part of journey

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the leg of the trip

parts.note: a stage is one leg of a journey
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Travellers needing somewhere for their bags partway through a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Room set aside for keeping bags and cases is storage space.

clue.text: Nobleman that is saint: before all others?

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A noble who is also a saint ranks ahead of everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming first in time, ahead of the rest, is what this superlative describes.

clue.text: Silly dopes wanting editor removed from office

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters of the next word are mixed up foolishly

explanation.surface: Foolish idiots want their editor sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' is the anagram signal on 'dopes', giving DEPOS; 'wanting' only links, it does not mean lacking here.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler or official forcibly ousted from power has been deposed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: My dear moving miles away

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of the preceding words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweetheart relocating far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lost in a daydream is said to be miles away, distracted and not paying attention.

clue.text: Shell that's yellow found by sea in France

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A golden shell picked up on a French beach.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an edible abalone of the Channel Islands, a mollusc with an ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Group of over-anxious characters rushed

indicators.note: a group of letters from the next word is taken out
characters means letters, so the group is of letters within the next word

explanation.surface: A band of nervy people hurried off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of ... characters' points to a run of letters inside 'over-anxious'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have run is the past of run, and hurrying is rushing.

clue.text: Friend is given minute token of victory

explanation.surface: A friend briefly receives a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm branch or frond was the classical prize symbolising triumph, so it stands for victory.

clue.text: Report of attempt to find adherent of religion

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken as said aloud

parts.note: to seek is to try to find

explanation.surface: A news story about a hunt for a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Sikhism, the faith founded by Guru Nanak in the Punjab.

clue.text: Nevertheless, creating a clash in the diary?

definitions.text: creating a clash in the diary?

explanation.surface: Despite everything, a double booking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means all the same, and literally describes two events booked for one moment.

clue.text: Decency of style associated with animal accommodation

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A tasteful, proper kind of fashion linked oddly to a farm building.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety in dress and behaviour, decorum, is the sense shared by these words.

clue.text: Bird or rabbit?

definitions.meaning: a small songbird such as the stonechat
in British slang to rabbit is to talk on and on, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk

explanation.surface: Is that creature feathered or furry?
explanation.definitionFit: The small songbird is named this, and British rhyming slang rabbit means talk, an informal natter.
